title: Collections Academy: Paid-in-Full Closure and Agency Referral of Deficiency Balance Accounts
content:
**The rule.** An account held under Deficiency Balance Accounts is paid in full on the day payments and credits bring its balance to zero; a paid-in-full letter is mailed within the band's letter period and the bureaus are updated within the band's bureau-update period with the paid-in-full status. An open account (not on a plan or settlement) that goes the band's referral period without a posted, unreturned payment is referred to an outside collection agency on that day and reported with the referral status; an account on a plan or settlement in force is never referred. A referred account stays with the agency, which alone takes payments and makes arrangements on it.

## Days without payment

The days without payment are the calendar days from the later of the opening date and the date of the latest posted payment that was not returned, to today.

## Questions answered by the rule

**When is an account paid in full?** On the day its balance reaches zero through payments and credits.

**Which accounts can be referred?** Only open accounts with no plan or settlement in force. An account on payment plan or on settlement plan is never referred, however long since its last payment.

**From which day are the days counted?** From the later of the opening date and the latest posted payment that was not returned. A returned payment does not count as a payment for this purpose.

**Who handles a referred account?** The agency alone; it takes the payments and makes any arrangement.

## Hypothetical illustration

An open account whose latest unreturned payment posted on a given day, under a 120-day referral period, is referred on the 120th calendar day after that payment if no further unreturned payment has posted; had the account been on a payment plan, it would not be referred.
